ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point b is on the left as the reference point, to the right of b there is a power source E1, labeled 10V, with polarity left negative and right positive; the right end of E1 is connected to node c through a 10Ω resistor R1. Node a is above, and there is a vertical 2Ω resistor R between a and c, with the current arrow downward. The upper branch to the right from a first passes through power source E2, labeled 8V, with polarity left positive and right negative, then passes through 4Ω resistor R2, to the right vertical power source E3; the upper end of E3 is marked negative, and the lower end is marked positive; the lower end of E3 then returns to node c through 2Ω resistor R3. Reasoning: Take Vb=0. From the polarity of E1, the potential of the node on the right side of E1 is +10V. Given Va=6V, let Vc be unknown, and let the current of the upper and right series branch from a to c be J. Write KCL for node a: the current leaving from a through the 2Ω resistor between a-c is (Va−Vc)/2, and the upper-branch current is J, so (Va−Vc)/2+J=0. Substituting Va=6 gives (6−Vc)/2+J=0. Write KCL for node c: the current to the +10V node through R1 is (Vc−10)/10, the current to a through the 2Ω resistor is (Vc−6)/2, while the upper-branch current J flows from a into c, so leaving this branch from c is −J, therefore (Vc−10)/10+(Vc−6)/2−J=0. Adding the two equations, (Vc−10)/10=0, therefore Vc=10V. Then from the node a equation, (6−10)/2+J=0, obtaining J=2A. Along the right branch from a to c, write the voltage relationship: passing through E2 from positive to negative drops 8V, passing through R2 drops 4J, passing through E3 from negative to positive is a rise of E3, namely the drop is −E3, and passing through R3 drops 2J, therefore Va−Vc=8+4J−E3+2J. Substituting Va−Vc=6−10=−4 and J=2 gives −4=8+8−E3+4=20−E3, so E3=24V.

method.method_draft: Set Vb=0 and from E1 polarity set the node to the right of E1 at +10 V. Let Vc be unknown and let J be the current through the upper/right series branch from a to c. Use the given Va=6 V. Write KCL at a and c to determine Vc and J; adding the KCL equations gives Vc=10 V, then KCL at a gives J=2 A. Traverse the right branch from a to c: drop 8 V across E2, drop 4J across R2, rise E3 across the vertical source, and drop 2J across R3. Equate this to Va−Vc and solve for E3=24 V.

method.method_draft: From the drawing, point b is a terminal with no other attached element, so KCL forces zero current through E1 and R1. Therefore R1 has zero voltage drop and node c is at the same potential as the positive terminal of E1, namely Vc=10 V relative to b. Node a is above, and there is a vertical 2Ω resistor R between a and c, with the current arrow downward. The upper branch to the right from a first passes through power source E2, labeled 8V, with polarity left positive and right negative, then passes through 4Ω resistor R2, to the right vertical power source E3; the upper end of E3 is marked negative, and the lower end is marked positive; the lower end of E3 then returns to node c through 2Ω resistor R3. Along the right branch from a to c, write the voltage relationship: passing through E2 from positive to negative drops 8V, passing through R2 drops 4J, passing through E3 from negative to positive is a rise of E3, namely the drop is −E3, and passing through R3 drops 2J, therefore Va−Vc=8+4J−E3+2J. Substituting Va−Vc=6−10=−4 and J=2 gives −4=8+8−E3+4=20−E3, so E3=24V.
